# What Dub API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. That run is sixteen characters and a body is twenty-four, so a
# body carries on through the alphabet to n. Where a case is about the ends of
# the alphabet rather than about the count, the run is shortened by however many
# characters the case writes at one end or the other, so that the body still
# comes to twenty-four.

patterns: dub-api-key

# The one prefix Dub issues an API key with. There is a single kind of string
# here rather than a table of them: a key carries whatever scopes it was created
# with and may be tied to a machine user rather than to a person, so nothing in
# the value says what it reaches, and the cases below are that one shape in the
# places a key is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       DUB_API_KEY=dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      DUB_API_KEY=«dub-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header the Dub API is called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      Authorization: Bearer «dub-api-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"token":"dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn"}
out:      {"token":"«dub-api-key»"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn" https://api.dub.co/links
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «dub-api-key»" https://api.dub.co/links

case:     a key in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"DUB_API_KEY": "dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn"}
out:      "env": {"DUB_API_KEY": "«dub-api-key»"}

case:     a key in yaml
in:       dub_api_key: dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_api_key: «dub-api-key»

case:     a key in a diff line
in:       +DUB_API_KEY=dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      +DUB_API_KEY=«dub-api-key»

case:     a key in a markdown code span
in:       `dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn`
out:      `«dub-api-key»`

# The alphabet the twenty-four characters are written in. It is base62 — the
# letters of both cases and the digits. The two characters base64url adds, the
# hyphen and the underscore, are not admitted, and either of them where a body
# stands is a body of fewer than twenty-four characters.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       dub_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMN
out:      «dub-api-key»

case:     a body opening on the last letter of the alphabet
in:       dub_z0123456789abcdefghijklm
out:      «dub-api-key»

case:     a body closing on the last letter of the alphabet
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmz
out:      «dub-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       dub_0123456789-bcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_0123456789-bcdefghijklmn

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       dub_0123456789_bcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_0123456789_bcdefghijklmn

case:     a hyphen straight behind the prefix
in:       dub_-123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_-123456789abcdefghijklmn

case:     an underscore straight behind the prefix
in:       dub__123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      dub__123456789abcdefghijklmn

case:     a space straight behind the prefix
in:       dub_ 123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_ 123456789abcdefghijklmn

# The lengths either side of twenty-four. The count is read exactly rather than
# as a floor, since it is the length Dub's own generator is called with, so
# twenty-three characters are not a key and twenty-five are a key and the
# character written after it.

case:     a body of twenty-four characters is a key
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      «dub-api-key»

case:     a body of twenty-three characters is not
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklm
out:      dub_0123456789abcdefghijklm

case:     an alphabet run longer than the count is a key and what follows it
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmno
out:      «dub-api-key»o

# The names ordinary code writes with these three letters. None of them reaches
# a body: a name is snake_case, and the underscore after its next word ends the
# run long before the twenty-fourth character. The shouted spelling is turned
# away by the case of the prefix instead.
#
# The second name is the first carried past the count, so that the characters
# the body test reads are all there and the underscore inside them is what
# rejects it. Both leave the text alone, and no out line can say which decided
# it; Test_DubAPIKey_holdsAKeyTheInputCutShort states that as the two offsets
# the scan settles at.

case:     a name whose segment closes on the prefix
in:       overdub_gain_factor = 2
out:      overdub_gain_factor = 2

case:     a name reaching past the count with an underscore inside it
in:       overdub_gain_factor_in_the_mixdown_settings = 2
out:      overdub_gain_factor_in_the_mixdown_settings = 2

case:     the prefix written in capitals
in:       DUB_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      DUB_0123456789abcdefghijklmn

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and the
# count ends it at its twenty-eighth character, so whatever is written after one
# stays in the text whether the alphabet admits it or not.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       DUB_API_KEY_dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      DUB_API_KEY_«dub-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xdub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      x«dub-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmnsuffix
out:      «dub-api-key»suffix

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn-suffix
out:      «dub-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn_suffix
out:      «dub-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn.
out:      the key is «dub-api-key».

case:     a key immediately against japanese on both sides
in:       鍵はdub_0123456789abcdefghijklmnです
out:      鍵は«dub-api-key»です

case:     a key against an invalid byte
in:       \xffdub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn\xff
out:      \xff«dub-api-key»\xff

# Two keys written together. The three letters the prefix opens with belong to
# the alphabet a body is written in, so a body may close with dub and the
# underscore of the next key stand directly behind it; the second key begins
# three characters before the first one ends, the two spans overlap and are
# redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between them the two keys are
# separate values, since the count ends the first one where the second opens.
#
# The prefix written twice is the same nesting with the outer candidate turned
# away: its body carries the underscore of the second prefix and so is no body,
# and the key stands four characters into the twenty-eight that candidate
# reached over. A scan stepping past a candidate it rejected would lose it.

case:     a key inside a candidate the body turned away
in:       dub_dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_«dub-api-key»

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijkdub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      «dub-api-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmndub_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMN
out:      «dub-api-key»«dub-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       dub_0123456789abcdefghijklmn dub_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMN
out:      «dub-api-key» «dub-api-key»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix closes with an
# underscore, which hexadecimal and standard base64 write nowhere, so only a
# base64url encoding can spell it — and where twenty-four letters and digits
# follow, those twenty-eight characters are redacted whether or not Dub issued
# them. Such a run is a key's format exactly and nothing in the text tells the
# two apart, so sparing it would spare a real key written the same way.
#
# The digest is the same over-match taking a value a reader had a use for.
# Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a digest carries nothing that ends a run, so
# every digest written behind the prefix is at least twenty-four characters: an
# MD5 is thirty-two, a SHA-1 forty and a SHA-256 sixty-four, and the first
# twenty-four of one go with the prefix while the rest of the digest stays. What
# holds either side of it is the count and the prefix — a run of sixteen is
# eight characters short of a body, and a hyphen is no character the prefix
# carries.
#
# The last case is the encoding that carries none of this. Standard base64
# writes + and / where base64url writes the hyphen and the underscore, so a
# certificate body holds no prefix to be found at however long it runs.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzdub_0123456789abcdefghijklmnzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«dub-api-key»zzzz

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzdub_0123456789abcdefghijklmnzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«dub-api-key»zzzz

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       dub_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «dub-api-key»89abcdef

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix in a cache key
in:       key: dub_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      key: «dub-api-key»89abcdef01234567

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix
in:       dub_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «dub-api-key»89abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a run of sixteen behind the prefix, eight characters short of a body
in:       dub_0123456789abcdef
out:      dub_0123456789abcdef

case:     an md5 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       dub-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dub-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a certificate body in standard base64
in:       MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEA0123456789abcdef+/0123456789abcdef
out:      MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEA0123456789abcdef+/0123456789abcdef

# The kinds Dub writes behind the same four characters that this pattern does
# not read. Each of them names its kind and closes that name with an underscore,
# so the twenty-four characters read behind dub_ run into a character no body
# admits — a rule that turns away a kind added tomorrow without its being
# written here, where these are the kinds Dub writes today.
#
# The embed token is the one whose body carries no run of its own: it is a ULID
# in Crockford's base32, which holds neither I nor L nor O nor U, so the run it
# is built from is the uppercase one with those four taken out.

case:     a publishable key
in:       dub_pk_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      dub_pk_0123456789abcdefghijklmn

case:     a public embed token
in:       dub_embed_0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRS
out:      dub_embed_0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRS

case:     an oauth client id
in:       dub_app_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dub_app_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an oauth client secret
in:       dub_app_secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      dub_app_secret_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     an oauth access token
in:       dub_access_token_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dub_access_token_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The prefix without the underscore it closes with, and a body of the right
# length with no prefix at all.

case:     the prefix without its closing underscore
in:       dub0123456789abcdefghijklmno
out:      dub0123456789abcdefghijklmno

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxx_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      xxx_0123456789abcdefghijklmn
